note: #91 (a fleet give-back reland of marching-arts' migration ladder + UTETY's user_version) stamped PRAGMA user_version into the store. IDEAS §6.31, the CHANGELOG's 'Not changed' note, and docs/releasing.md had all deliberately RESERVED store-schema-versioning as 'a decision to be argued rather than slipped into another change' — and #91 slipped it in. Caught while preparing the 0.2.0 release commit: the CHANGELOG line 'No store schema version' was now false. Surfaced to the operator, who ratified deliberately (this record is that argument, made explicit rather than buried). The store half is settled here; the ledger half of §6.31 stays open and unstamped.

decisions.question: Should the store carry a schema version (PRAGMA user_version), which §6.31 reserved as a decision to be argued, not stamped inside another change?
decisions.commitment: Yes — ratified as of 0.2.0. The store now carries user_version = SCHEMA_VERSION (1), with an ordered forward-migration ladder (empty today) and a fail-closed refusal of a newer-than-known file (StoreSchemaTooNewError). This is exactly the 'schema generation in the database' §6.31 named as the STRONG fix for the §6.8 warm-connection hazard (a pooled connection skips a migration it did not have when opened). §6.31's own text said the store half 'touches no hash chain, so the argument it needs is small' — this record is that small argument, made. Not extended to the ledger: a hash chain cannot be re-hashed under new rules, so its format is already frozen by its first entry and versioning it is a separate, larger decision that stays open.
decisions.why: The mechanism was welcome — §6.31 anticipated it verbatim ('a user_version would make the migration a decision about a number rather than an inference from a shape'). The defect was the FORM: it arrived undocumented, inside a give-back batch, contradicting a CHANGELOG line. The honest repair is not to revert good, tested work (11 migratability/refusal tests, effective-schema digest unchanged) but to make the deferred argument explicit and record it where the next cold agent will find it. Reverting would re-open a gap the repo had already decided it wanted closed; deferring the whole tag would hold the fleet give-back on @master for a decision §6.31 said was small. The line that stays bright: the ledger is not versioned, because that argument is genuinely still open.
